item.title: Government to spend 15 billion DKK on coastal protection to prevent flooding
item.description: The Danish government will spend nearly 15 billion DKK from 2029 to 2040 on dikes, storm surge walls, and other forms of protection along the country’s coasts. item.title: Denmark still has a problem with second-generation immigrants being forcefully sent to their parents’ country for “re-education” trips
item.description: Children in Denmark are still being sent abroad against their will, even though the practice is illegal. A new report shows that so-called re-education trips continue to affect young people, girls in particular, and often involve years of social control before they are forced to leave to environments that put their health and development at risk.

item.title: Novo stock closes at 2021 low on weight loss data
item.description: Novo Nordisk’s B-share fell over 16 percent to 251.4 DKK, its lowest closing price since June 2021. The decline followed study data for the weight-loss drug Cagrisema, which showed a 23 percent weight loss over 84 weeks. In comparison, Eli Lilly’s tirzepatide achieved 25.5 percent weight loss. item.description: The North Denmark Regional Council has appointed Swedish provider Premedic as the new supplier for ambulance and patient transport services in Himmerland, Han Herred, Thy, and Mors. item.title: Minister backs new model for ash scattering rules
item.description: Minister for Ecclesiastical Affairs Morten Dahlin reports broad support for modernizing Denmark’s burial law and rules regarding ash scattering. Current regulations prohibit scattering ash over land, dividing remains, or keeping urns at home.
